why: A = telescopeProj_comp_telescopeMap ∧ IsHomotopyEquiv.of_telescopeMap (universes 0). A ⇒ B uses A's second clause after transporting along the identity homeomorphism tel S ≃ₜ telescope S (Homeomorph.setCongr; the sets are equal but not definitionally): fSig = telescopeMap and telProj = telescopeProj up to it, IsHE ↔ IsHomotopyEquiv, IsHDL S ↔ Monotone S ∧ IsHomotopyDirectLimit S; B's formula for f_Σ and p_Y ∘ f_Σ = f ∘ p_X are rfl. B ⇒ A holds on the common domain of increasing sequences (B_to_A_mono, uses B), but A's of_telescopeMap is stated for arbitrary (non-monotone) sequences, which B (whose IsHDL includes monotonicity) does not cover; the general case is Milnor's 2-out-of-3 argument (f ≃ f∘p_X∘s = p_Y∘f_Σ∘s), proved outright in B_to_A without using B. So A is formally slightly more general, by a hypothesis-free argument; on Milnor's setting they are equivalent.
overlap: B_to_A / B_to_A_mono share only basic telescope lemmas (mem_telescope, mem_telescope_map, telescopeMap/telescopeProj proof fields) and the generic IsHomotopyEquiv.comp / of_homotopyEquiv / exists_homotopyEquiv / of_homotopic with the formal proofs.
embedded_special_case_note: General topology (telescopes, homotopy equivalences); no Riemannian manifold.
